newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares slip in thin trade volume.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares slip in thin trade volume.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Thursday in thin trade with trading limited to local operators while Western investors mostly stayed away from the market, traders said.
They forecast a further fall during the day.
"We shall close two to three percent lower on yesterday's close," said Andrei Ippolitov, IK Prospekt corporate securities director. "We have already done half of the fall."
Trinfiko trader Ilya Galtsov said he saw big Western sales in long-distance telephone company Rostelekom RTKM.RTS, but could not say why.
Rostelekom fell to $3.42 from $3.46 at Wednesday's close.
Ippolitov said GAZ GAZA.RTS automaker was in renewed demand due to the government's plans to supply its employees with local cars instead of foreign ones.
GAZ rose to $42.50 from $40.00.

Traders said Western investors were mostly staying away from the market and concentrating on buying rare shares, like small and medium-size machine-building and helicopter companies and hydro-power stations.
Galtsov said the news power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS plans to issue $150 million of five-year Eurobobonds in the second of third quarter of 1997 prevented the share from falling lower than it did.

Mosenergo chief executive Nestor Serebryanikov said the company would drop controversial plans for a new share issue fi the Eurobond and a $150 million loan from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development go ahead successfully.
"Now Mosenergo and (national power utility) UES EESR.RTS have a chance to change to uptrend," said Galtsov.
Mosenergo was $1.230 after $1.229 and UES fell to $0.2100 from $0.2109.
But Ippolitov said the Eurobond news was unlikely to affect Mosenergo.
"Of course, in general it's good, but not enough to push the price anywhere," he said.
"The company will raise more funds and will pay higher dividends. Maybe later, when all the market will start growing, Mosenergo will grow 0.5 percent quicker than the others."
He said the market had already discounted news that Nizhnervartovskneftegaz NZGZ.RTS oil company plans to issue 1.0 billion new shares.
Nizhnevartovskneftegaz was $7.4 after $7.5 on April 17, when it was last traded.
Ippolitov said there would be no Western demand before the Western markets calmed down and showed a clear trend.
"People are nervious, that's why they think it is better not to buy Russia," he said.
--Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
